inputs.title: The Thing
inputs.logline: When Bo’s big tail betrays how hard it is to meet new friends, Keen and Aida help him discover that the very thing he wants to hide may be the first thing everyone loves.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.storyBeat: Keen attempts an exaggerated stealth mission toward Fuzzby’s honeycomb, but every crunchy step and snore-bubble pop makes the world more awake than he wants it to be. The beat is about borrowed boldness meeting tiny physical resistance.
beats.want: Keen wants to get close enough to take honey without waking Fuzzby.
beats.need: He needs to learn that rushing toward what he wants is not the same as being ready or unseen.
beats.kidRead: Keen is being silly-sneaky and the sleeping bee might wake up any second.
beats.adultRead: A child’s confidence is charmingly exposed by his own body and the environment; he is not as invisible as he thinks.
beats.emotionalIntent: Light suspense and giggly anticipation, with the honeycomb as the forbidden prize.

beats.adultRead: The comedy is the impossibility of controlling every tell; Keen’s cover is doomed because he is still a kid in a too-big plan.
beats.emotionalIntent: Build the laugh through anticipation, release it with the sneeze, then button it with Fuzzby’s sleepy authority.

beats.need: She needs to trust the quiet signal and make room for someone else’s fear without taking over.
beats.kidRead: A magic bowl shows a squirrel who keeps packing but does not go anywhere.
beats.adultRead: The repetition is instantly recognizable as a child trying to make a hard transition feel controllable.
beats.emotionalIntent: Quiet wonder with a small ache under it; the vision should feel intimate, not flashy.

beats.storyBeat: Inside the hollow tree, Bo answers his offscreen Mum but bargains with time and his conker, delaying the Learning Circle by making “a minute” stretch absurdly. The safe room is cosy, but it is also a trap of postponement.
beats.want: Bo wants to put off leaving while sounding like he still intends to go.
beats.need: He needs to be witnessed in the stuck place instead of left alone with the loop.
beats.kidRead: Bo keeps finding reasons not to go yet, and his conker is like his little helper.
beats.adultRead: The offscreen parent call captures the morning-transition ache: encouragement from another room cannot cross the threshold for him.
beats.emotionalIntent: Tender comic avoidance; keep it small, domestic and recognisable.

vision.premise: Bo is due at the Learning Circle for the first time, but every step toward the door makes his tail poof with worry. Keen’s playful curiosity and Aida’s quiet truth help him move toward the group one step at a time, until the tail he feared becomes his way in.
vision.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo go to the Learning Circle without having to hide the part of himself that gives him away?
vision.theme: Belonging begins when the thing you were trying to hide is gently witnessed and welcomed.
vision.externalJourney: Keen fails to steal honey, is redirected by Aida, visits Bo’s hollow tree, walks him through the woods, helps him arrive at the Learning Circle, and returns home to find Fuzzby attempting his own honey heist.
vision.internalJourney: Bo moves from delaying and controlling every detail to taking a visible step forward with his worry still present, then letting his tail become play instead of proof that something is wrong with him.
vision.relationshipChanges: Bo and Keen shift from strangers at a doorway to easy friends; Bo and Aida move from cautious distance to shared truth; Bo and the Learning Circle group move from imagined judgement to delighted acceptance. Fuzzby and Zenny provide the comic echo: being ridiculous and still belonging.
vision.emotionalCurve: Playful mischief opens the episode, then narrows into Bo’s held-at-the-door worry. The woods give relief through play, dip again at the log, soften through Aida’s honesty, glow into the walk forward, burst into group joy, and settle in a warm, lightly comic garden coda.
vision.comedyCurve: The comedy starts with stealth, snore bubbles, pollen and sneezes; turns into tail-poof escalation and Keen’s useless-tail demonstration; blooms into group delight at the Learning Circle; and ends with Fuzzby’s flower-disguise failure and Zenny’s tiny crack of amusement.
vision.setupPayoffMap: The untouched honeycomb and Fuzzby’s “never ever” return in the final garden heist. Bo’s conker and repeated packing plant his need for control. The tail’s first unwanted poof pays off as a chosen game in the woods and then as the Learning Circle’s delight. Aida’s vision of Bo unable to move pays off in Bo walking forward under pink and blue light. “Every single time” moves from Aida’s truth to Bo’s own action phrase.
vision.visualMotifs: Closed/open thresholds, paws holding objects too tightly, Bo’s tail expanding beyond his control, the forest path as a visible line between home and belonging, and the honeycomb as comic temptation that remains untouched.
vision.sonicMotifs: Crunching steps, snore-bubble pops, sneeze blasts, the shave-and-a-haircut knock, tail POOFs, Aida’s bowl tone, rose and aquamarine glow tones, group cheers, and Zenny’s bookend Ommmm.
vision.climax: Aida and Keen each offer their crystal truth, pink and blue light join on the forest path, and Bo takes one step, then another, toward the Learning Circle.
vision.resolution: At the Learning Circle, Bo’s tail poofs in front of everyone and is met with wonder, cheering and play; later, he draws with Keen while Aida watches his settled belonging from the edge of the clearing.
vision.intendedFinalFeeling: Warm, giggly relief: the child feels the fun of the fluffy tail, while the adult feels the ache of a child being welcomed without needing to edit himself.

northStar.surfaceStory: Bo hides in his hollow oak and keeps delaying the Learning Circle, until Keen arrives, sees the tail-poof Bo fears, and reacts with wonder instead of judgement.
northStar.universalTruth: When a child is scared of being too noticeable, one delighted witness can make the same exposed part feel less dangerous — not fixed, just survivable enough to take the next step.
northStar.childClearWant: Bo wants to stay inside, keep his tail normal, and make today turn into tomorrow.
northStar.emotionalNeed: Bo needs to be seen kindly before he can risk being seen by everyone.
northStar.falseBeliefUnderPressure: If my tail does the THING, nobody will like me.
northStar.relationshipEngine: Keen changes the scene by not trying to calm Bo down or explain bravery; he simply enters Bo’s closed loop, gets startled with him, then genuinely loves the thing Bo is trying to hide.
northStar.ordinaryLifeTruth: “I’ll do it in a minute” can be a child’s way of holding a big scary doorway shut.
northStar.sceneTurn: The tail does the dreaded THING, but Keen’s impressed stare and “Whoa. Your tail is AMAZING.” flip the meaning from shame to possibility.
audienceJourney: Giggly recognition: Bo is obviously stretching time with the conker and the minute.
Playful suspense: the doorway gets closer, but Bo’s thoughts keep bouncing him back.
Sudden startle: Keen’s cheerful arrival breaks the private worry-loop.
Tiny gasp: Bo finally says the fear and the tail betrays him right away.
Relief-laugh: Keen’s own tail demonstration is proudly unimpressive.
Warm lift, not full cure: Bo can go for a walk with one friend, but the Learning Circle fear is not solved yet.
northStar.finalAfterFeeling: Airier and less trapped; Bo is still nervous, but now his nervousness has company.
northStar.dialogueSubtractionOpportunity: Do not add any line explaining that Keen has made Bo feel accepted. Keep the approved dialogue verbatim, and let the silence after Keen’s amazed look, Bo’s small checking glance, the tail’s changed weight, and Bo’s growing smile carry the shift.
northStar.environmentPressure: The hollow oak is cosy enough to protect Bo and small enough to trap him: the door frames the outside as a test, the satchel and conker become a postponement machine, and the tail has too little room to hide once the fear is spoken.

tapestry.physicalMotif: The conker-and-satchel loop: in, out, in, out — Bo’s thoughts made physical. It should begin as comic delay, tighten into stuckness, then settle once Keen’s company interrupts the loop. The tail-poof is the involuntary truth that the conker cannot contain.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.storyBeat: Keen attempts an exaggerated stealth mission toward Fuzzby’s honeycomb, but every crunchy step and snore-bubble pop makes the world more awake than he wants it to be. The beat is about borrowed boldness meeting tiny physical resistance.
beats.want: Keen wants to get close enough to take honey without waking Fuzzby.
beats.need: He needs to learn that rushing toward what he wants is not the same as being ready or unseen.
beats.kidRead: Keen is being silly-sneaky and the sleeping bee might wake up any second.
beats.adultRead: A child’s confidence is charmingly exposed by his own body and the environment; he is not as invisible as he thinks.
beats.emotionalIntent: Light suspense and giggly anticipation, with the honeycomb as the forbidden prize.

treatments.name: The Room That Keeps Shrinking
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience feels trapped inside Bo’s postponement machine: funny at first because “a minute” is being stretched with a conker and a satchel, then a little breath-held as the same cosy room starts to feel too small for the fear he is trying to contain. Keen’s arrival should feel like someone opening a window in the middle of a thought-loop.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: Bo governs the scene. The camera does not diagnose him; it shares the physical experience of delay — the door is close, the outside is bright, the conker is manageable, and the Learning Circle is too big to step toward yet. Keen is experienced first as interruption, then as relief.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Comic mechanism: escalating overcommitment through the conker-and-satchel loop. Each attempt to make “today” smaller makes Bo’s stuckness more visible. Dramatic mechanism: the room’s snug safety becomes pressure; the turn is Keen’s genuine wonder reframing the tail-poof from exposure to possibility.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Bo’s body keeps voting before his words do: paws busy with the conker, shoulders and breath tightening near the doorway, retreating into tasks whenever the outside gains importance. His lines should ride stop-start thought, not polished explanation. Keen arrives open and forward, not as a fixer; he is bright, curious, and then honestly impressed. His stare after the tail-poof must be clean wonder, not politeness. Bo’s change is small: a checking glance, a softened hold in the body, then the smile beginning because he believes one person might mean it.
treatments.visualGrammar: Compressed, close interior grammar. The hollow oak is warm but crowded in the frame: satchel, conker, doorway edge, Bo’s own tail-space all press into him. Early compositions let objects interrupt Bo, as though his delaying tools are now blocking him. The doorway’s daylight is present but not yet welcoming. After Keen’s “AMAZING,” the same light loosens the space; the room does not change, but the frame breathes.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera is caught in Bo’s loop. It circles back to the satchel with him, catches the conker as if it matters too much, and hesitates at the doorway when he does. When Keen knocks, the camera is startled with Bo rather than safely waiting for Keen. After Keen’s impressed look, the camera stops chasing objects and stays with Bo’s processing.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Bo supplies fidgeting movement: in, out, in, out; step, stop, retreat. The decisive stillness arrives when the loop becomes real stuckness at the door. Keen’s entrance breaks that stillness with forward energy, but the most important stillness is his amazed stare after the poof. That held attention is what lets Bo stop fighting himself for a breath.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Depth carries pressure. Foreground objects — conker, satchel flap, doorway rim — repeatedly make the path out feel segmented. The outside sits in bright depth beyond the door, initially too large to enter. When Keen appears, the doorway depth becomes relational: not “the world judging Bo,” but one friend standing close enough to see kindly.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: Begin with playful repetition: Bo answers Mum, buys a minute, works the conker. The rhythm tightens as the door nears and his thoughts swing between okay/not okay. Keen’s knock creates a sharp comic rupture and scramble. Bo’s fear speech accelerates until the tail does the thing. Then the scene must drop into a tiny quiet after Keen’s wonder before the release-laugh of Keen’s uneventful demonstration and the gentle walk offer.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are motivated by changed pressure, not coverage. Cut when the conker becomes the thought, when the doorway becomes the obstacle, when Keen’s arrival changes the room’s ownership, when the tail-poof changes the truth, and when Keen’s unimpressive tail becomes the joke. Avoid routine shot/reaction machinery; Bo’s loop can hold longer until it stops being funny and becomes stuck.
treatments.openingImage: Warm interior close on the conker caught between Bo’s paw and the satchel mouth, with the open doorway only a bright slice beyond him — a whole day reduced to one tiny postponement object.
treatments.closingImage: Bo and Keen sharing the threshold, the satchel no longer dominating Bo’s hands, the doorway now wide enough for two small bodies and one still-nervous next step toward fresh air.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Do not make the hollow oak merely cosy. The danger is a cute room with cute business. The frame must prove that comfort can become a trap: close foregrounds, low ceiling-feel, and doorway brightness that pressures Bo before it welcomes him. I will resist any safe, static two-character staging once Keen arrives; the space must visibly reassign itself from Bo’s loop to shared company.

treatments.name: The Doorway Learns to Be Kind
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience watches the meaning of one doorway transform. At first, it is the scary line between Bo’s private room and the public Learning Circle. By the end, it is the place where Keen stands with him, so stepping out becomes less like being exposed and more like being accompanied.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: The scene is governed by the threshold rather than by a single face. Bo’s fear is measured by how far he can get toward the door; Keen’s kindness is measured by what his presence does to that same doorway. The audience always understands the geography: inside is safety-with-stuckness, outside is risk, and Keen becomes the bridge.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Dramatic mechanism: environmental redefinition. The exact same architectural feature changes emotional job without being explained. Comic mechanism: anticipation and reversal — the doorway seems to promise danger, but the interruption that comes through it is Keen’s friendly knock and a conker-juggling scramble, followed by his proudly useless tail comparison.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Bo treats the door like it can hear his bargaining. He approaches it in fragments, then pulls his attention back to the conker whenever the outside gets too real. His fear line should feel like it escapes before he can tidy it. Keen’s performance is simple and direct: he arrives because Aida sent him, takes in Bo’s panic without making it worse, and reacts to the tail with delighted truth. No soothing performance, no lecture posture — his help is attention, play, and an invitation to move.
treatments.visualGrammar: Threshold grammar. Frames are organized by inside/outside contrast, not by conventional talking positions. Doorlight draws a shape across the floor that Bo crosses, avoids, or gets caught beside. Before Keen, the outside is over-bright and slightly intimidating; after he stands there, that light wraps into the room and reveals more air around Bo. The final visual rhyme should make the opening doorway fear recognizably changed.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera behaves like the doorway has a point of view: sometimes looking inward at Bo’s delaying rituals, sometimes just inside with him looking outward, sometimes caught on the line between. Keen’s arrival is not pre-covered; the camera may be with Bo’s hands or the doorlight when the knock interrupts, then find Keen as Bo does.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Bo’s movement is back-and-forth across the threshold zone without fully committing. Keen’s movement is clean arrival: forward, uncomplicated, not pushy. Stillness matters at two thresholds: Bo frozen before the door when the loop stops being a game, and Keen frozen in wonder after the tail-poof. The first stillness traps; the second stillness witnesses.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Use the hollow oak as a tunnel of feeling. Interior depth is shallow and object-heavy when Bo delays; exterior depth beyond the door is bright and unreadable. Keen standing in that depth gives it scale and friendliness. By the end, the door no longer divides foreground Bo from background world; it holds Bo and Keen in one shared plane of intention.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: Start airy and playful with offscreen Mum and Bo’s “minute.” Let each return to the satchel make the room feel a little more circular. As Bo reaches the door, slow the rhythm enough for the audience to sense that tomorrow is a hiding place, not a plan. Keen’s knock should land as comic surprise. The tail-poof creates the tiny gasp. Keen’s “AMAZING” releases the room, then the nothing-tail demonstration gives the laugh back quickly.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are doorway turns: inside task, doorway pressure, outside interruption, shared seeing, exit offer. Do not cut just because a new line begins. Dialogue can play across held visual pressure if the doorway is actively changing meaning. The most important cut may be away from Bo’s panic to Keen’s unguarded wonder, because that is the altered power in the scene.
treatments.openingImage: Bo inside the hollow oak with the doorway bright behind or beside him, his attention turned away from it toward the conker — the exit present, but not yet usable.
treatments.closingImage: The doorway holding Bo and Keen together, daylight no longer a glare but a path, with Bo’s choice still small and nervous enough to remain honest.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: The easy version is to stage this as an interior conversation with a door in the background. I reject that. The door is the scene’s emotional machine. Every composition must ask: is the threshold dividing, threatening, interrupting, witnessing, or inviting right now? If we cannot read that change without added explanation, the treatment has failed.

treatments.name: The Thing Takes the Truth
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience enjoys a suspense game around the unseen or half-seen tail: Bo is trying to keep the “THING” out of the scene, but the scene keeps making room for it. Children get the delicious wait for the poof; adults feel the ache of a child trying to hide the part of himself that will not obey.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: The emotional point of view belongs to Bo’s involuntary truth — the tail as the part of him that cannot perform “normal” on command. Bo’s face and hands try to manage the day; the tail and crystal-world logic tell us what is actually happening underneath. Keen’s role is to look at the exposed truth without fear.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Comic mechanism: concealment to revelation. The tail is avoided, blocked, tucked out of priority, or crowded by satchel business until Bo names the fear and it immediately does the dreaded thing. Dramatic mechanism: shame turns into wonder because Keen’s first full read of the tail is admiration rather than judgement.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Bo performs management: keep hands busy, keep the conker important, keep the tail normal, keep today postponed. When he blurts the fear, the performance cracks and the tail answers before he can recover. His “Stop it!” is not anger at the tail; it is a small plea to the part of himself he cannot control. Keen must not overplay amazement. His “Whoa” starts as genuine intake, then “AMAZING” lands as plain fact. His own tail demonstration is proudly offered and completely uneventful, making the comparison funny without mocking Bo.
treatments.visualGrammar: Selective-reveal grammar. Early frames privilege hands, satchel, door, and Bo’s attempts to occupy himself, while the tail is cropped, hidden behind furniture, or felt as offscreen pressure in the composition. The audience senses there is a secret in the frame before it is fully paid off. When the poof happens, the frame must finally give the tail honest space instead of treating it like a mistake.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera is curious but not cruel. It notices Bo avoiding the tail and lets the audience anticipate the reveal, but it does not leer at his embarrassment. It may drift toward the tail before Bo wants it to, be pulled back by the conker loop, then commit fully when the thing happens. After Keen’s line, the camera’s relationship changes: it looks at the tail the way Keen does — with permission and delight.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: The hiding is busy; the truth is sudden. Bo’s paws and attention keep moving to distract from the part he fears. The tail-poof interrupts that busy management with one clear physical event. The held stillness after Keen sees it is essential: no quick gag should trample the moment when Bo realizes the look he feared is not the look he got. Then movement returns as Keen demonstrates his own nothing-tail and invites a walk.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Use depth to make hiding imperfect. The satchel and conker can dominate the foreground while the tail’s space is squeezed in background or edge-depth. Doorlight can catch the tail before Bo wants it seen. The hollow oak’s curved walls should make concealment difficult: there is no perfect corner for the truth to disappear into. Once Keen admires it, the frame gives Bo, Keen, and the tail enough shared air to coexist.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The scene begins as misdirection: conker business seems to be the joke. The rhythm then reveals that the conker is a decoy for a bigger worry. As Bo’s lines move from tomorrow-bargaining to “What if nobody likes me,” the hidden subject becomes unavoidable. The poof is the single turn. Keen’s wonder creates the tiny gasp of relief, and his own tail’s non-event restores comedy within seconds.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cut to reveal withheld information, not to cover dialogue. Early cuts may avoid the tail as Bo avoids it. Once the fear is named, the cut logic flips: the frame must show the consequence cleanly and then privilege Keen’s seeing. The release gag gets its own clean visual idea — Keen’s demonstration — because it is not an extension of Bo’s shame; it is the scene handing laughter back to him.
treatments.openingImage: A tight, busy image of Bo’s conker and satchel activity arranged so that the tail’s place in the room is conspicuously denied — the secret is present because the frame is working so hard not to look at it.
treatments.closingImage: Bo no longer arranged to hide the tail, standing with Keen in a room that has made space for the thing and for the next step outside.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: The risk is either hiding the tail so well that the audience has no anticipation, or showcasing it so early that Bo’s fear has no engine. The camera must calibrate partial knowledge: enough absence to make children lean in, enough restraint to protect Bo’s vulnerability, and one decisive reveal when the script earns it. No neutral medium staging will carry that.

treatmentSelection.selectedTreatment: The Room That Keeps Shrinking, governed through the changing doorway
combinedFrom: The Doorway Learns to Be Kind
Selective-reveal calibration from The Thing Takes the Truth only as a secondary tool
treatmentSelection.governingAudienceExperience: The audience should feel Bo’s funny little delay game slowly become a too-small room, then feel one bright breath of relief when Keen’s delighted witnessing turns the doorway from exposure into company.
treatmentSelection.rationale: Select Treatment 1 as the spine because it puts us inside Bo’s postponement machine: conker, satchel, doorway, tail-space, repeat. That is the clearest emotional truth of the scene — not “Bo is nervous,” but “Bo is making today smaller because the outside feels too big.” It gives comedy from behaviour, not business, and it protects Bo’s specificity: his paws keep solving the wrong problem while his body keeps telling the truth. Combine Treatment 2’s doorway grammar because the threshold is the scene’s visual promise and payoff; the same door must begin as a test and end as a shared way out. Use Treatment 3 only in restraint: partial tail-awareness can build anticipation, but the scene must not become a tail-reveal suspense machine. The turn belongs to Keen’s kind seeing of Bo, not to the object lesson of the tail. This combination gives the strongest co-viewing experience: children laugh at the conker loop, the knock-scramble, the poof, and Keen’s unimpressive demonstration; adults feel the ache of a child trying to delay being seen. The camera’s job is experiential, not illustrative: it gets caught in Bo’s loop, is startled by Keen, then finally stops chasing objects when Bo is witnessed. The scene ends warmer but not cured — Bo can step out with one friend, not magically conquer the Learning Circle.
treatmentSelection.rejectionChecks: No selected element may depend on fixed character lanes; Bo and Keen must not be assigned permanent sides of the frame. No requirement to keep all characters visible; absence, obstruction, hands, doorlight, satchel, and tail-space are allowed to carry pressure. Reject habitual action/reaction coverage: the cut logic follows changing emotional pressure, not each new line. Reject safe camera placement: Keen’s knock must interrupt the camera’s attention rather than arrive into pre-arranged coverage. Reject repeated close-up punctuation; the turn is held in relational seeing and changed space, not a series of face-buttons. Reject mechanical shot counts; rhythm is governed by the loop tightening, rupture, tiny quiet, release-laugh, and shared exit. Reject generic “cinematic” treatment language unless it becomes observable staging pressure. Reject merely illustrating the script; every frame must answer what the conker, the room, the doorway, and Keen’s attention mean to Bo right now. Treatment 3 is rejected as the governing approach because making the tail the primary POV risks turning Bo’s shame into a reveal device; its selective-reveal idea is useful only if it remains subordinate to Bo’s relationship with Keen and the doorway’s emotional transformation.

shots.purpose: Carry the full postponement loop from comic bargaining to genuine stuckness under one compressed interior reference regime.
shots.audienceExperience: The audience starts giggling at Bo stretching a minute with a conker, then feels the room grow smaller when the doorway is finally close enough to cross.
shots.openingImage: Warm interior close on the conker caught between Bo’s paw and the satchel mouth, with the open doorway only a bright slice beyond him.
shots.principalPerformance: Bo’s body votes against his words: busy paws, a freeze at the door, then faster conker choices as the thought-loop overtakes him.
shots.cameraRelationship: The camera is trapped in Bo’s loop, giving the conker importance because Bo does, then hesitating at the doorway with him.
shots.physicalOrEmotionalChange: The hollow oak changes from safe hideaway to pressure chamber, and the conker changes from lunch-bag business to fear-management tool.
shots.closingImage: Bo near the open doorway with the conker gripped outside the satchel, the bright exit close but uncrossed.

cinematographyContract.memorableLandingImage: Bo holding the conker outside the satchel at the bright threshold, caught between task and day.
cinematographyContract.providerInstruction: Start tight on conker and satchel inside the hollow; follow Bo’s attention as he answers Mum, approaches the bright doorway, freezes, retreats and repeats the conker in-out loop until he ends clutching it at the uncrossed door.

performanceBudget.rationale: Two causal stages fit under 30 seconds: the comic delay and the threshold panic. The repeated conker business needs room to change meaning, but it does not require a split before Keen arrives.

storyIntent.narrativeFunction: Establish the fear as postponement behaviour before the fear is named.
storyIntent.primaryAudienceFeeling: Giggly recognition turning into small concern.
storyIntent.secondaryAudienceFeeling: Adult recognition of a child using ‘a minute’ to hold a big day away.
storyIntent.outerAction: Bo answers Mum, handles the conker and satchel, reaches the door, freezes and retreats into the conker loop.
storyIntent.innerAction: He tries to shrink the Learning Circle into one controllable object and discovers the object cannot make today safe.
storyIntent.performanceDirection: Play each task as a thought arriving through the paws; the voice should be stop-start bargaining rather than a planned speech.
storyIntent.mutedRead: With sound off, the audience sees a child promise readiness while his body keeps choosing the conker over the doorway.
storyIntent.environmentPressure: The hollow’s warm closeness becomes too snug; the door, satchel flap and foreground clutter physically segment his escape path.
storyIntent.soundStory: Mum’s offscreen call creates outside pressure; conker clacks and satchel rustles make the delay machine audible.
storyIntent.motifUse: The signed motif is the conker-and-satchel loop: in, out, in, out as Bo’s thoughts made physical.
storyIntent.thoughtChangeAndCut: Bo’s thought changes from ‘I can buy a minute’ to ‘I cannot cross today’; the cut is motivated once the private loop is fully stuck and ready to be broken from outside.
storyIntent.mustUnderstand: Bo is not lazy; he is scared and using tiny tasks to delay a too-large social moment.
storyIntent.mustNotKnowYet: The exact feared tail-poof and Keen’s kind reaction are not revealed yet.
storyIntent.reactionBeat: Bo’s freeze at the doorway changes the meaning from playful delay to real anxiety.
storyIntent.relationshipDistance: Mum remains offscreen and caring but distant; Bo is alone with the pressure.
storyIntent.relationshipPowerDynamic: Mum’s call has practical authority, but Bo controls the room by postponing until the doorway takes power from him.
storyIntent.touchOrAvoidance: Bo clings to conker and satchel instead of touching the doorway or stepping through it.
storyIntent.eyelineRule: Bo’s eyeline keeps dropping to the conker whenever the doorway becomes too much.
storyIntent.silhouetteRead: A small stalled figure at a bright opening with a round object held close.
storyIntent.silenceRule: Protect the freeze before the panic line; let the room go tight rather than filling it with extra business.
storyIntent.scoreInstruction: Withhold score or keep it minimal under room sounds; allow only a faint unresolved pulse as the doorway pressure grows.

shots.physicalPerformance: Bo keeps the conker and satchel working long after he has responded to Mum, then reaches the doorway and locks up. His paws hover, retreat to the satchel, change the conker’s place again and again, and finally clamp it close beside the uncrossed light.
shots.animationTiming: Begin with small, fussy paw business and soft satchel rustles; let the doorway freeze land as a held stop. The later conker moves tighten and shorten, ending with a breath-held landing hold at the threshold.

performanceContract.playableIntention: Bo is trying to make the big outside day small enough to control by keeping one object-task active.

Bo places the conker away, moves to the doorway, opens toward the light, then stops with his shoulders pulled up and his paws suspended between the exit and the satchel.

performanceContract.requiredLanding: The audience must read Bo as scared rather than lazy: a small figure at the bright opening, holding the conker because the doorway is too much to cross.
performanceContract.performanceFreedom: Allow variation in paw fidgets, eye darts, breath catches, satchel flap movement and tail tension, as long as the conker remains the readable thought-object and the freeze clearly changes the comic rhythm into pressure.

voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Briefly hopeful, but fragile enough to crack immediately.
voicePerformances.pace: Slower than the previous line; each word placed carefully.
voicePerformances.rhythm: A small step forward, almost whispered to the threshold.
voicePerformances.pauses: Micro-pause before “OK,” as if checking whether the word will hold.
voicePerformances.breaths: Gentle inhale before the line; let the breath almost disappear at the end.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Paws nearly stop; conker held close beside the uncrossed light.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: The stiller body lets the voice try on courage; the line is a fragile pause in the fidgeting.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Begin during the breath-held landing hold at the threshold, after the last conker adjustment has stopped.

voicePerformances.speaker: Bo
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Bo — courage snaps into a panic squeak before he can stop it.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Pull Mum, the room, and himself back from the terrifying possibility of today.
voicePerformances.subtext: I tried being brave and it made the scary thought louder.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Mum and the doorway at once; he needs someone to catch the fear he just revealed.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Startled by his own panic, locked at the threshold.
voicePerformances.pace: Fast burst, then cut off hard.
voicePerformances.rhythm: One thought detonating; no tidy shape.
voicePerformances.pauses: No internal pause; the panic has no brakes.
voicePerformances.breaths: Caught breath before “What”; end slightly breathless.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Paws clamp the conker close; body freezes at the threshold.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: The vocal rupture is the inside of the doorway freeze finally escaping.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Hit immediately after the fragile hold from the previous line, as the thought-loop overtakes him.

voicePerformances.speaker: Keen
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Keen — open, forward, friendly without noticing he has arrived at maximum volume for Bo’s nerves.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Make contact quickly and make himself easy to like.
voicePerformances.subtext: New friend! This is simple, right?
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Bo at the doorway; Keen assumes welcome before he reads the fear.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Still bright, beginning to register Bo’s startled reaction.
voicePerformances.rhythm: A friendly pop-in; one bright wave of sound.
voicePerformances.pauses: No pause after the line number; keep the greeting immediate.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Keen appears with crisp forward energy; Bo jolts and the conker pops loose.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: Keen’s easy arrival causes Bo’s physical rupture; the voice should feel harmless but too sudden for Bo.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Land on the doorway appearance/knock rupture, just before or as the conker pops loose.

voicePerformances.speaker: Keen
voicePerformances.exactDialogue: Aida sent me. She thought we should meet.
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Keen — sincere messenger, trying to make the surprise feel official and safe.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Reassure Bo that this visit has a kind reason behind it.
voicePerformances.subtext: You are not in trouble; someone thought of you.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Bo, now visibly startled; Keen softens his forward energy toward him.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Curious and more attentive to Bo’s reaction.
voicePerformances.pace: Moderate, less bouncy than the greeting.
voicePerformances.rhythm: Two simple facts, offered gently; the second sentence warms.
voicePerformances.pauses: Small pause after “me.” to let Bo catch up.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Bo fumbles through delayed paw corrections; Keen remains forward but begins reading the room.
voicePerformances.elevenLabsV3Direction: Aida sent me. She thought we should MEET.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: The voice softens because Bo’s body has exposed distress; Keen is trying not to crowd him further.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Start after the conker pop and first fumble catch, giving Bo’s jolt room to play.

voicePerformances.speaker: Bo
voicePerformances.exactDialogue: What if nobody likes me at the Learning Circle? I don't think I can go today. What if my tail does the THING?
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Bo — startled into honesty, words spilling faster than his paws can organise them.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Make Keen understand the danger before Keen can expect him to go.
voicePerformances.subtext: If I say all the scary parts first, maybe you won’t laugh when they happen.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Keen; Bo is testing whether this new bear is safe enough to hear the truth.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: More panicked, physically crowded by his own tail.
voicePerformances.pace: Too fast, uneven; the middle sentence tries to become firm, then fear surges again.
voicePerformances.rhythm: Spill, brace, spike. Not polished; it should feel blurted.
voicePerformances.pauses: Tiny breath-pause after the first question; press through the second sentence; a dread-filled lift before “THING.”
voicePerformances.breaths: Shallow, repeated catch-breaths; let the final question ride on a near-squeak.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Bo fumbles the conker, hugs it, then his tail expands and crowds him.
voicePerformances.elevenLabsV3Direction: [nervous] What if nobody likes me at the Learning Circle? I don't think I can go today. What if my tail does the THING?
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: The voice exposes the fear at the same time the body exposes it; tail expansion is the fear becoming visible.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Begin after Bo hugs the conker. The final “THING” should coincide with or slightly follow the first soft comic force of the tail expansion.

voicePerformances.speaker: Bo
voicePerformances.exactDialogue: Stop it! Please just be a normal tail!
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Bo — pleading with his own body, mortified that Keen is watching.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Command the tail to stop revealing him and beg it to let him look ordinary.
voicePerformances.subtext: Don’t show him how scared I am.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: His tail first, Keen second; Keen’s gaze makes the plea sharper.
voicePerformances.pace: First phrase pops hard; second phrase collapses into pleading speed.
voicePerformances.pauses: Sharp break after “Stop it!”; no extra pause in the plea.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Bo wrestles the expanding tail; it continues to crowd him with soft comic follow-through.
voicePerformances.elevenLabsV3Direction: Stop it! [gulps] Please just be a NORMAL tail!
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: The voice tries to control what the body cannot; the failed control is the comedy and the vulnerability.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Place “Stop it!” on the first tail crowding beat; “normal tail” should land while he is still wrestling it, not after he succeeds.

voicePerformances.speaker: Keen
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Keen — clean, genuine amazement; not teasing, not fixing, just delighted truth.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Let Bo know the thing he fears is actually wonderful to Keen.
voicePerformances.subtext: I see the part you’re hiding, and I like it.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Bo, with full attention; Keen has gone still so Bo can trust the admiration.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Still, sincere, inviting Bo to believe him.
voicePerformances.pace: Slow enough for real wonder; no salesmanship.
voicePerformances.rhythm: A hushed discovery followed by clear admiration.
voicePerformances.pauses: Meaningful pause after “Whoa.” to let the amazement land as observation, not reaction noise.
voicePerformances.breaths: Soft inhale before “Your tail,” as if choosing honesty carefully.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Keen becomes still with clean amazement; Bo checks the look for judgement.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: Keen’s stillness makes the praise safe; the quieter voice proves he is not performing excitement at Bo.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: After the tail’s soft follow-through settles. Hold the protected quiet on Keen before “Your tail.”

voicePerformances.speaker: Bo
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Bo — guarded, tiny hope peeking out from behind embarrassment.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Ask Keen to confirm the praise without making Bo look like he needs it.
voicePerformances.subtext: Please mean it. Please don’t take it back.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Keen; Bo is checking Keen’s face as much as his words.
voicePerformances.emotionalEntry: Braced for laughter, surprised by admiration.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Only a little softened; still protected.
voicePerformances.pace: Very gentle, hesitant, almost too quiet.
voicePerformances.rhythm: A delayed opening; the thought arrives before the voice.
voicePerformances.pauses: Honor the leading ellipsis as a real hesitation before “you.”
voicePerformances.breaths: Small held breath, then a soft release into the question.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Bo checks Keen’s amazed stillness and softens only a little.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: The voice is a cautious crack in the armour while the body remains protective around the conker and tail.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Do not rush after Keen’s compliment. Let Bo’s eye-check land first; speak on the first tiny softening.

voicePerformances.speaker: Keen
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Keen — cheerfully self-unimpressed, using his own non-event to make Bo feel less alone.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Reframe Bo’s fear by offering a silly comparison instead of advice.
voicePerformances.subtext: You’re not weird to me; if anything, I’m the boring one.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Bo, who is testing whether Keen’s admiration is real.
voicePerformances.emotionalEntry: Sincere admiration turning into playful reassurance.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Proudly ready to demonstrate something that will not happen.
voicePerformances.rhythm: Set-up line with a tiny proud button on “Watch.”
voicePerformances.pauses: Small pause between sentences for Keen to turn and prepare the demonstration.
voicePerformances.breaths: Easy breath before “Watch,” like he is presenting a trick.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Keen turns with cheerful confidence and prepares the tail demonstration.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: The voice sets up the physical gag with total confidence, making the coming non-event funnier and kinder.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: After Bo’s guarded belief-test hold. “Watch” lands as Keen finishes turning into position.

voicePerformances.speaker: Keen
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Keen — delighted by the anticlimax, sharing the joke without making himself the victim.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Use the failed demonstration to gently loosen Bo’s shame.
voicePerformances.subtext: See? Bodies do funny things, or don’t. We can survive it.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Bo; Keen wants Bo to laugh with him, not at him.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Warmly amused, leaving space for Bo’s smile to build.
voicePerformances.rhythm: Tiny reveal, then a deadpan button.
voicePerformances.pauses: Important comic pause after the wiggle/non-event before “See?”; short pause before “Nothing.”
voicePerformances.breaths: No big breath; keep it light and unforced.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Keen wiggles, presents the unchanged tail, then holds the non-event cleanly.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: The pause lets the unchanged tail be the joke; the voice simply buttons what the body already showed.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Do not speak until after the proud wiggle and a clean hold on the unchanged tail.

voicePerformances.speaker: Keen
voicePerformances.exactDialogue: Let’s go for a walk and get some fresh air. Fresh air always helps.
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Keen — practical, warm, offering movement instead of a lecture.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Invite Bo into a small next step that does not sound like going to the Learning Circle yet.
voicePerformances.subtext: We don’t have to solve today from the doorway. We can just move together.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Bo, whose smile is still forming and still nervous.
voicePerformances.emotionalEntry: Playful reassurance after the tail gag.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Confident but not triumphant; ready to leave beside Bo.
voicePerformances.rhythm: Invitation first, reassurance second; the repeated “Fresh air” should feel like Keen’s simple rule of life.
voicePerformances.pauses: Small pause after the first sentence to check Bo is still with him.
voicePerformances.breaths: Open, relaxed breath before the invitation.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Keen’s confidence turns outward toward the exit while leaving room for Bo to choose.
voicePerformances.elevenLabsV3Direction: Let’s go for a WALK and get some fresh air. Fresh air always helps.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: The voice supports the modest shared exit; it offers a walk, not a victory march.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Begin after Bo has compared tails and his own tail has started to deflate; finish before the exit fully commits.

voicePerformances.speaker: Bo
voicePerformances.voiceIdentity: Bo — still nervous, but surprised to find the next step is small enough to hold.
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Accept Keen’s invitation without pretending all the fear is gone.
voicePerformances.subtext: I can do a walk. Maybe that can become the next thing.
voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Keen; Bo is giving him a little trust.
voicePerformances.emotionalEntry: Cautiously warmed by the gag and the praise.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: Willing to move, with nervousness still present.
voicePerformances.pace: Soft, slower than Keen; a small smile audible by the end.
voicePerformances.rhythm: Careful agreement that opens as it goes.
voicePerformances.pauses: Tiny thought-pause before the line; no internal pause.
voicePerformances.breaths: Gentle exhale into “That,” like releasing one held worry.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Bo takes the satchel as luggage and leaves beside Keen, modestly rather than triumphantly.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: The exhale lets the body unclamp; the voice and the small satchel-taking action mark believable willingness.
voicePerformances.expectedTiming: Start as Bo’s smile becomes fuller and he takes the satchel; let “nice” carry into the modest shared exit.

northStar.theme: Belonging begins when the thing you were trying to hide is gently witnessed and welcomed.
northStar.childClearWant: Bo wants to stay inside, keep his tail normal, and make today turn into tomorrow.

scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.purpose: Bo’s postponement loop turns from funny delay into visible fear, then Keen’s delighted witnessing makes the doorway feel survivable enough for Bo to share a next step.
scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo risk being seen outside when the thing he wants to hide may happen in front of someone?
scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.entry: I am safer if I delay today and keep the THING hidden.
scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.exit: He accepts the walk for fresh air and lets the doorway become a shared way out rather than a wall.

pointOfView: Bo’s postponement machine; the room is experienced as his manageable objects becoming too many edges.
Bo’s experience of being interrupted, exposed, then unexpectedly witnessed kindly.
Bo processing Keen’s admiration until it becomes a small accepted step.

dramaticBeats.beginning: Bo reduces the whole Learning Circle day to one small postponement object; the hollow oak begins as safety but starts to read as a place built for delay.
dramaticBeats.development: The private postponement machine breaks. The doorway now contains a specific friend, not the whole judging world.
dramaticBeats.turn: Bo asks if Keen truly thinks so; Keen demonstrates his own uneventful tail, names the nothingness, and offers fresh air; Bo lets the idea land and agrees.
dramaticBeats.landing: The release-laugh of Keen’s proudly unimpressive tail hands into a warm lift: Bo can go outside with one friend, still nervous but accompanied.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Bo’s body votes against his words: busy paws, a freeze at the door, then faster conker choices as the thought-loop overtakes him.
performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: Bo keeps the conker and satchel working long after he has responded to Mum, then reaches the doorway and locks up. His paws hover, retreat to the satchel, change the conker’s place again and again, and finally clamp it close beside the uncrossed light.

contract.playableIntention: Bo is trying to make the big outside day small enough to control by keeping one object-task active.

phases.observableAction: Bo stays low over the satchel, keeping the conker between his paws while the bright doorway remains behind him and off to the side.
Bo places the conker away, moves to the doorway, opens toward the light, then stops with his shoulders pulled up and his paws suspended between the exit and the satchel.
Bo scurries back into the hollow, takes the conker out, puts it back, then pulls it out again with quicker, less tidy paw corrections.
Bo ends near the doorway gripping the conker in both paws outside the open satchel, with the exit close and still uncrossed.

contract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Mum’s offscreen call pulls Bo toward leaving; the doorway light makes the outside immediate; Bo’s body redirects that pressure into the conker-and-satchel loop, so each object change delays rather than advances the exit.
contract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Bo changes from busy, contained stalling to a full threshold freeze, then to hurried object handling that no longer looks playful or useful.
contract.requiredLanding: The audience must read Bo as scared rather than lazy: a small figure at the bright opening, holding the conker because the doorway is too much to cross.
contract.performanceFreedom: Allow variation in paw fidgets, eye darts, breath catches, satchel flap movement and tail tension, as long as the conker remains the readable thought-object and the freeze clearly changes the comic rhythm into pressure.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Supplied scene canon: Bo’s body votes before his words do; under pressure he retreats into paws-busy tasks and checks small objects instead of stepping toward the larger fear.
characterTruths.playableWant: Keep the Learning Circle day at a distance by making the conker and satchel feel more urgent than the doorway.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: He tightens at the threshold, drops his attention back to the conker, and repeats the satchel action with increasing speed and less control.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Busy paws, caught breath, raised shoulders, doorway avoidance, repeated conker state changes, and a final two-paw clutch near the exit.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Keen would move forward with open curiosity, and Mum would supply practical outside pressure; only Bo turns one small object into a postponement machine and physically freezes at the door.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Bo is startled into exposure, then blurts too much too fast; Keen remains forward, curious and finally still with real admiration.
performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: Keen appears at the doorway with easy forward energy, and Bo jolts so sharply the conker pops loose. Bo fumbles it through delayed paw corrections, hugs it, then exposes the fear physically as his tail expands and crowds him. Keen becomes still with clean amazement; Bo checks that look and softens only a little.

contract.playableIntention: Bo loses control of the private thing he feared, and Keen’s honest wonder gives the exposed tail a safer meaning.

phases.observableAction: Keen’s shadow crosses the doorway before he leans in with an open, forward posture and a light tapping gesture on the hollow tree.
Bo jerks upward; the conker springs from his paws, bounces between paw, satchel flap and air, and ends locked against his chest.
Bo’s tail expands suddenly behind him; he grabs and guards it, then is crowded again as it expands a second time and fills more of the hollow space.
Keen holds completely still with bright, focused attention on the enlarged tail, then keeps that delighted attention available for Bo’s checking glance.

contract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Keen’s doorway tap interrupts Bo’s tight object loop, causing the conker to pop loose and making Bo’s panic visible. When Bo’s tail expands, the small room confirms the exposure by running out of tail-space; Keen’s still gaze then becomes the action that changes how the room feels.
contract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Bo moves from startled concealment to exposed guarding; Keen’s still, delighted attention shifts the exposure from something Bo fights to something he can briefly look back from.
contract.requiredLanding: The final read must be Bo with an enlarged tail still present, Keen admiring without teasing, and the room loosened by the fact that being seen has not driven Keen away.
contract.performanceFreedom: Give animators freedom in the exact conker bounces, Bo’s grip adjustments, tail fur follow-through and Keen’s micro-smile, but keep Bo’s scramble unskilled, the tail involuntary, and Keen’s reaction sincere and still.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Supplied scene canon: Keen arrives open, forward, bright and curious; he helps by genuine interest rather than fixing or lecturing.
characterTruths.playableWant: Enter the room as friendly company and meet Bo without making Bo a problem to solve.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: He stays easy at the doorway during the scramble, then becomes still when the tail expands, letting wonder rather than advice fill the pause.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Forward lean, unembarrassed entrance, open attention, then a clean held stare at the tail with no recoil and no invasive touch.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Bo would guard and retreat from the exposure; Aida would anchor with quiet elder stillness. Only Keen breaks the loop with bright arrival and then reframes the tail through amazed curiosity.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Supplied scene canon: Bo’s fear shows through involuntary body action; his tail reveals what he cannot keep managed.
characterTruths.playableWant: Hide the embarrassing body reaction and recover control before Keen can judge it.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: He clutches the conker, grabs the tail, tries to compress himself around it, and repeatedly checks Keen’s face for the result of being seen.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Startle jump, frantic delayed catches, conker hug, tail-guarding paws, crowded posture, and small checking glances toward Keen.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Keen would not turn exposure into a guarded retreat, and Mum is not physically present in the room; only Bo’s fear converts into the conker scramble and involuntary tail expansion.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Bo’s change is small and believable: guarded check, almost-smile, fuller smile, then a still-nervous willingness to move.
performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: Bo stops wrestling the tail and watches Keen for proof. Keen turns with cheerful confidence, wiggles, and presents a tail that remains completely unchanged. Bo compares Keen’s tail with his own; his tail deflates, his smile builds, and he takes the satchel as luggage before leaving beside Keen.

contract.playableIntention: Bo is testing whether Keen’s admiration can be trusted, then accepting a small shared step outside instead of retreating into the loop.

phases.observableAction: Bo releases his grip on the tail, keeps his body guarded, and looks from the enlarged tail to Keen’s face for confirmation.
Keen turns to show his own tail, gives his body a confident little wiggle, and lets the tail hang completely still.
Bo looks from Keen’s still tail to his own; his tail slowly settles smaller, his shoulders lower, and the first smile begins.
Bo lifts the satchel without cycling the conker, steps into the doorway beside Keen, and moves out with his tail settled behind him.

contract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Keen’s deliberately ordinary tail demonstration gives Bo a safe comparison. Seeing no spectacle from Keen lets Bo stop fighting his own tail; the tail deflates, the satchel becomes something to carry, and the doorway becomes a shared path.
contract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Bo changes from guarded checking to a small smile and a willing step; the satchel loses its role as a delay device and becomes ordinary travel weight.
contract.requiredLanding: End on Bo and Keen sharing the threshold, with Bo still gentle and cautious but moving outside with company, not cured or pushed.
contract.performanceFreedom: Allow flexibility in Bo’s tiny smile build, the pace of tail deflation, Keen’s proud comic posture and secondary satchel motion, as long as the non-event reads clearly and Bo’s exit remains a small chosen step.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Supplied scene canon: Bo changes in small, believable increments; his body softens only after he has checked whether safety is real.
characterTruths.playableWant: Believe Keen’s admiration enough to stop guarding the tail and try one step outside with him.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: He checks visually before relaxing, compares the two tails, lowers his shoulders, lets the tail settle, and handles the satchel normally.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Guarded glance, hands leaving the tail, slow tail deflation, growing smile, normal satchel lift, and a careful shared step through the doorway.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Keen would lead with bright action, not cautious belief-testing; only Bo needs the comparison to turn guarded stillness into a small accepted exit.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Supplied scene canon: Keen offers silliness and company instead of instruction; his confidence is open and not self-protective.
characterTruths.playableWant: Make room for Bo to feel less alone by sharing a playful, unimpressive comparison and then offering movement together.
characterTruths.pressureResponse: He cheerfully demonstrates his own tail without embarrassment and keeps the invitation light, leaving Bo room to choose.
characterTruths.observableSignature: Easy turn, confident wiggle, tail staying unchanged, proud pause on the non-result, and relaxed readiness to walk beside Bo.
characterTruths.substitutionTest: Bo could not make the non-event reassuring because he is the one being exposed; Aida would steady the room differently. Only Keen can turn his own lack of spectacle into a friendly release-laugh.

camera.shotScale: Object-close to compressed small-body threshold framing, never a roomy master.

camera.cameraHeight: Low inside the hollow at Bo’s working height, rising only enough to register the doorway as a taller demand.
camera.composition: Satchel flap, conker and doorway rim repeatedly interrupt Bo rather than framing him comfortably.
camera.depthStrategy: Foreground delay objects segment the path; the outside stays bright in depth and emotionally too big.
camera.cameraBehavior: Circles back when Bo circles back, stops when he freezes, and lets the last panic land without tidying the frame.
camera.focusStrategy: Focus follows Bo’s attention between conker, satchel and doorway; rack only when his thought genuinely shifts.
camera.lightingFunction: Warm interior sunlight protects him at first, while the doorway light presses brighter and less cosy as he nears it.
camera.paletteFunction: Honeyed wood tones hold safety; the doorway’s fresher exterior colour remains present but intimidating.
camera.performanceVisibility: Hands, breath, shoulder tension and doorway hesitation must stay readable; facial acting supports the physical loop.
camera.editorialPurpose: Earn the cut to Keen by completing Bo’s private stuckness before anyone else enters.
camera.memorableLandingImage: Bo holding the conker outside the satchel at the bright threshold, caught between task and day.
camera.providerInstruction: Start tight on conker and satchel inside the hollow; follow Bo’s attention as he answers Mum, approaches the bright doorway, freezes, retreats and repeats the conker in-out loop until he ends clutching it at the uncrossed door.

stages.observableEndState: The conker sits as the main thing in Bo’s paws while the open doorway remains secondary and far too bright.

stages.purpose: Let the conker loop stop being only funny and become real stuckness at the threshold.
stages.primaryEvent: Bo reaches the door, freezes, then repeatedly changes the conker’s state between satchel and paws as his spoken thoughts swing from tomorrow to today to panic.
stages.emotionalOrComicTurn: The rhythm tightens from giggle to breath-hold when the door proves harder to cross than Bo’s bargaining can manage.
stages.cameraAndTransition: Move with Bo toward the door, then stop hard when he freezes; circle back with the conker only because his attention does, compressing foreground satchel, doorway rim and Bo’s tail-space around him.
stages.observableEndState: Bo is stalled at the doorway with the conker clutched out of the satchel, the bright outside pressing at his side.

stages.emotionalOrComicTurn: The private anxiety becomes visible to someone else before Bo can manage it.

stages.emotionalOrComicTurn: The breath-held fear softens because the witness loves the exposed thing.
stages.cameraAndTransition: Let the camera stop chasing Bo’s objects and hold the relational line between Keen’s amazed attention and Bo’s checking glance.
stages.observableEndState: Bo remains nervous but visibly softened, with Keen’s kind attention holding the room open.

internalShots.purpose: Let the fear speech and tail-poof be one cause-and-effect exposure.

internalShots.storyAction: Keen looks impressed and names the tail as amazing; Bo processes whether the admiration is real.
internalShots.performanceFocus: Keen’s stillness must be honest wonder, not politeness; Bo’s softening is tiny and cautious.
internalShots.landingImage: Keen’s delighted attention held on Bo’s tail while Bo’s guarded posture begins to loosen.
internalShots.cutReason: The next unit needs a fresh comic reset for Keen’s uneventful tail demonstration; staying continuous would crowd the quiet after the emotional reversal.

stages.emotionalOrComicTurn: The panic gives way to a tiny searching hope.

stages.observableEndState: Bo and Keen share the threshold and begin out toward fresh air, with Bo’s tail settled and his bag carried along.

performances.emotionalExit: Still delaying, with the thought-loop beginning to tighten.

shots.purpose: Carry the full postponement loop from comic bargaining to genuine stuckness under one compressed interior reference regime.
shots.audienceExperience: The audience starts giggling at Bo stretching a minute with a conker, then feels the room grow smaller when the doorway is finally close enough to cross.
shots.openingImage: Warm interior close on the conker caught between Bo’s paw and the satchel mouth, with the open doorway only a bright slice beyond him.
shots.principalPerformance: Bo’s body votes against his words: busy paws, a freeze at the door, then faster conker choices as the thought-loop overtakes him.
shots.cameraRelationship: The camera is trapped in Bo’s loop, giving the conker importance because Bo does, then hesitating at the doorway with him.
shots.physicalOrEmotionalChange: The hollow oak changes from safe hideaway to pressure chamber, and the conker changes from lunch-bag business to fear-management tool.
shots.closingImage: Bo near the open doorway with the conker gripped outside the satchel, the bright exit close but uncrossed.

cinematographyContract.performanceVisibility: Hands, breath, shoulder tension and doorway hesitation must stay readable; facial acting supports the physical loop.
cinematographyContract.editorialPurpose: Earn the cut to Keen by completing Bo’s private stuckness before anyone else enters.
cinematographyContract.memorableLandingImage: Bo holding the conker outside the satchel at the bright threshold, caught between task and day.
cinematographyContract.providerInstruction: Start tight on conker and satchel inside the hollow; follow Bo’s attention as he answers Mum, approaches the bright doorway, freezes, retreats and repeats the conker in-out loop until he ends clutching it at the uncrossed door.

performanceBudget.rationale: Two causal stages fit under 30 seconds: the comic delay and the threshold panic. The repeated conker business needs room to change meaning, but it does not require a split before Keen arrives.

storyIntent.narrativeFunction: Establish the fear as postponement behaviour before the fear is named.
storyIntent.primaryAudienceFeeling: Giggly recognition turning into small concern.
storyIntent.secondaryAudienceFeeling: Adult recognition of a child using ‘a minute’ to hold a big day away.
storyIntent.outerAction: Bo answers Mum, handles the conker and satchel, reaches the door, freezes and retreats into the conker loop.
storyIntent.innerAction: He tries to shrink the Learning Circle into one controllable object and discovers the object cannot make today safe.
storyIntent.performanceDirection: Play each task as a thought arriving through the paws; the voice should be stop-start bargaining rather than a planned speech.
storyIntent.mutedRead: With sound off, the audience sees a child promise readiness while his body keeps choosing the conker over the doorway.
storyIntent.environmentPressure: The hollow’s warm closeness becomes too snug; the door, satchel flap and foreground clutter physically segment his escape path.
storyIntent.soundStory: Mum’s offscreen call creates outside pressure; conker clacks and satchel rustles make the delay machine audible.
storyIntent.motifUse: The signed motif is the conker-and-satchel loop: in, out, in, out as Bo’s thoughts made physical.
storyIntent.thoughtChangeAndCut: Bo’s thought changes from ‘I can buy a minute’ to ‘I cannot cross today’; the cut is motivated once the private loop is fully stuck and ready to be broken from outside.
storyIntent.mustUnderstand: Bo is not lazy; he is scared and using tiny tasks to delay a too-large social moment.
storyIntent.mustNotKnowYet: The exact feared tail-poof and Keen’s kind reaction are not revealed yet.
storyIntent.reactionBeat: Bo’s freeze at the doorway changes the meaning from playful delay to real anxiety.
storyIntent.relationshipDistance: Mum remains offscreen and caring but distant; Bo is alone with the pressure.
storyIntent.relationshipPowerDynamic: Mum’s call has practical authority, but Bo controls the room by postponing until the doorway takes power from him.
storyIntent.touchOrAvoidance: Bo clings to conker and satchel instead of touching the doorway or stepping through it.
storyIntent.eyelineRule: Bo’s eyeline keeps dropping to the conker whenever the doorway becomes too much.
storyIntent.silhouetteRead: A small stalled figure at a bright opening with a round object held close.
storyIntent.silenceRule: Protect the freeze before the panic line; let the room go tight rather than filling it with extra business.
storyIntent.scoreInstruction: Withhold score or keep it minimal under room sounds; allow only a faint unresolved pulse as the doorway pressure grows.

shots.physicalPerformance: Bo keeps the conker and satchel working long after he has responded to Mum, then reaches the doorway and locks up. His paws hover, retreat to the satchel, change the conker’s place again and again, and finally clamp it close beside the uncrossed light.
shots.animationTiming: Begin with small, fussy paw business and soft satchel rustles; let the doorway freeze land as a held stop. The later conker moves tighten and shorten, ending with a breath-held landing hold at the threshold.

performanceContract.playableIntention: Bo is trying to make the big outside day small enough to control by keeping one object-task active.

Bo places the conker away, moves to the doorway, opens toward the light, then stops with his shoulders pulled up and his paws suspended between the exit and the satchel.
Bo scurries back into the hollow, takes the conker out, puts it back, then pulls it out again with quicker, less tidy paw corrections.
Bo ends near the doorway gripping the conker in both paws outside the open satchel, with the exit close and still uncrossed.

performanceContract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Mum’s offscreen call pulls Bo toward leaving; the doorway light makes the outside immediate; Bo’s body redirects that pressure into the conker-and-satchel loop, so each object change delays rather than advances the exit.
performanceContract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Bo changes from busy, contained stalling to a full threshold freeze, then to hurried object handling that no longer looks playful or useful.
performanceContract.requiredLanding: The audience must read Bo as scared rather than lazy: a small figure at the bright opening, holding the conker because the doorway is too much to cross.
performanceContract.performanceFreedom: Allow variation in paw fidgets, eye darts, breath catches, satchel flap movement and tail tension, as long as the conker remains the readable thought-object and the freeze clearly changes the comic rhythm into pressure.

characterTruths.observableSignature: Busy paws, caught breath, raised shoulders, doorway avoidance, repeated conker state changes, and a final two-paw clutch near the exit.

showrunnerJudgement: PASS. The scene preserves the selected experience: Bo’s delay starts as recognisable child-comedy, tightens into a physically trapped doorway-loop, then releases through Keen’s delighted witness rather than through explanation. The child-clear want is visible in behaviour — Bo keeps today small with the conker, satchel and threshold avoidance — and the costly choice lands when he blurts the real fear in front of Keen. Keen’s function is right: not therapist, not bravery coach, but an open interruption who becomes relief because his amazement is genuinely observational. The final movement toward fresh air keeps the fear alive enough; it does not falsely solve the Learning Circle.
treatmentComparison: This storyboard remains closely aligned to “The Room That Keeps Shrinking.” The conker-and-satchel loop is not decorative; it is Bo’s postponement machine. The hollow oak is treated as warm but pressurised, with foreground objects and doorway brightness segmenting the path out. The camera relationship also follows the treatment: caught in Bo’s object-loop first, startled by Keen rather than safely waiting for him, then calmer after Keen’s “AMAZING.” The strongest match is the intended redefinition of the doorway: first exposure, then company. The scene also appears legible muted: Bo stalled at the threshold with conker/satchel and bright outside pressure would read without dialogue, and Keen’s still amazed attention after the poof carries the turn in staging rather than explanation.
packingJudgement: Packing passes. Three Seedance units are justified: S3.SH1 at 28s carries the delay-to-stuckness arc; S3.SH2 at 27s carries interruption-to-tail-wonder; S3.SH3 at 21s carries belief-testing, comic release and shared exit. The adjacent joins are not avoidable under the 30-second rule because SH1+SH2 and SH2+SH3 would exceed the limit, and each split protects a real change in dramatic ownership. The cards are dense but within the stated stage/internal-shot limits, and the split logic does not appear to create empty padding.
